en.title: Google OA #41: Maximum Score with Blocked Following Indices
en.description: Given an array points, the value at each index is the score for that position. If you take the score at an index whose value is v, then the v indices immediately after it can no longer be taken (only later indices are affected). Find the maximum total score you can obtain.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains n integers points[0..n−1]. 1≤n≤200000, 0≤points[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output one integer, the maximum total score.
en.explanation:
Example 1: in [25,1,3,99,4], take the 1 at index 1 (blocking index 2), then take the 99 at index 3, for 100 in total.
Example 2: in [0,4,0,5], taking a position with value 0 blocks no index; taking 5 (and the two 0s) gives 5, while taking 4 would block the 0 and the 5 after it.
Example 3: in [2,1,1,1,6], taking the 2 at index 0 blocks indices 1 and 2; then take the 6 at index 4, for 8 in total.
hints: After taking index i, the next index that can be taken is i+points[i]+1.
Do dynamic programming from right to left.
Positions with value 0 do not block any index.
